title: Gaps in work after the Sterling Club
summary: Smith presses for what came after the Sterling Club; Lovett remembers little except that the band did not last and he was off a while.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, any way, from there did you keep
Then where did you -- what did you do after that? We're up to '47, '48 now.
We were all (inaudible). Ain't nothing happened, as I know of. I assume.

Well, you couldn't be off for too long, you have to work, you know, I mean, and you've got the biggest name in Kansas City jazz for the last 30, 40 years around town, you know. You couldn't have been unemployed too long.
Every time I turn around you were working in a different room and I wish I got the booking instead of you, you know, even today.
You know, some of the best cats were off, man. Benny Goodman and everybody else.
Oh, everybody gets off, I know that. You can't work all the time. Unfortunately -- so what is the next gig that you remember after the Sterling Club?
After the Sterling Club? Oh, man.
It would be the late forties.
It's hard for me to remember way back then.
We're getting pretty close, it's only 25, 26 years.
After the Sterling Club -- did I tell you I was with Julia before then?
Yeah, you were with Julia before then then she went to the Cuban Room and you got a band together to go out to the Sterling Club.
Yeah. That band didn't last too long I know that. But I don't remember just what happened after that. I know I was off for a while.
